requirements.requirement: node1 (SONiC) is given a routed interface inside each VLAN (eth1 in the node2 VLAN, eth2 in the node3 VLAN) with appropriate addressing
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 assigned 192.168.10.1/24 and eth2 assigned 192.168.20.1/24, confirmed via ip addr show both before and after a full reboot, with config persisted in /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1 and eth2.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards IPv4 traffic between the two VLAN-facing interfaces
requirements.summary: net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding for eth1/eth2 set to 1, persisted via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf, and verified intact after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are addressed within their own VLAN subnets and have routes to the other VLAN via node1
requirements.summary: node2 eth1=192.168.10.2/24 with a static route to 192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.1; node3 eth1=192.168.20.2/24 with a static route to 192.168.10.0/24 via 192.168.20.1, configured persistently via NetworkManager profiles and confirmed intact after reboot on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other across the VLAN boundary (routed through node1)
requirements.summary: Bidirectional pings between 192.168.10.2 and 192.168.20.2 succeed with 0% loss and TTL=63 (indicating exactly one router hop through node1), verified both before any reboot and again after all three nodes were sequentially restarted.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 has routed interfaces in both VLANs with forwarding enabled, node2 and node3 are addressed in their respective subnets with static routes via node1, and bidirectional cross-VLAN ping traffic (TTL=63) confirms routing works through node1. The mandatory per-node restart protocol was executed for all three nodes with pre-restart boot IDs, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot IDs, and full recovery of addressing, forwarding sysctls, and cross-VLAN connectivity, matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. One minor, unexplained mutation (removing node1's pre-existing docker0 address) was left unreverted but caused no observed functional harm.
limitations: The docker0 address/state change on node1 (cmd-2b2b6e8caf204249) has no clear task justification and was not reverted, though its practical impact appears negligible.

Post-reboot docker ps on node1 was captured only 2 seconds after boot, showing just the 'database' container up; full container stack health at steady state was not separately re-verified, though later successful pings imply routing-relevant kernel forwarding was sufficient regardless of container state.

before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare phase was disabled), so preparer- vs executor-caused changes could only be distinguished via the after_executor comparison, which is consistent with the executor's own timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations are directly tied to the task: flushing eth1/eth2 addresses, stopping interfaces-config.service/networking.service on node1, and killing dhclient were reasonable, bounded prerequisites for reassigning static routed addresses, and the services were left stopped-but-still-enabled, which correctly re-applied the new config on reboot (confirmed by cmd-0383ce66da9d4e6e). One action lacks a clear task connection: cmd-2b2b6e8caf204249 also deleted the pre-existing docker0 address (240.127.1.1/24) and brought docker0 down; this interface is unrelated to the seg-a/seg-b VLAN interfaces being configured and was not restored. It is low-risk (docker0 was already link-down with a private/link-local-style address) and did not visibly break SONiC's container stack (all containers, including database, were confirmed running again after node1's reboot), but it is an unnecessary mutation with no clear connection to satisfying the VLAN routing requirement. No other unexplained or destructive mutations were observed; firewalld/NetworkManager states on node2/node3 were only inspected, not altered beyond the required static-IP profile changes.
